design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (water_mitigation_billing), revision 2. Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[6,4,6]; taken as water_ext_drying_deposit=6, water_ext_tearout_antimicrobial=4, water_ext_tearout_debris=6.
WHY A GOOD TEST: a self-pay landlord asks only to pay what lets the crew set drying equipment. The scored figure (the amount collected, 14273.16) is fixed only after two hidden, record-visible obligations are booked: the tear-out debris haul-off line and the tear-out antimicrobial line (both owed because the job carries pad removal and flood cut lines dated 2026-09-14 and no debris_haul / antimicrobial line). Each line is a multi-factor price; the deposit stacks a six-factor IICRC drying estimate, a 60 percent share, the tier floor, every posted charge and the posted customer payment.
SCOPE: task 0 claims water_ext_tearout_debris, water_ext_tearout_antimicrobial, water_ext_drying_deposit and tools book_tearout_debris_a8b773d4, book_tearout_antimicrobial_173ee43e, pay_drying_deposit_ee9a2909. Task 1 (disjoint) claims water_ext_final_hepa_vacuum and water_ext_insured_share with book_final_hepa_eb899e1c and pay_insured_share_cc172b06.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root water_ext_drying_deposit (owner=user tool). Edge 1 deposit<-debris, value_input, gate charges_posted, form state, sentence "On a job carrying pad removal, carpet removal or flood cut lines, the amount collected before drying equipment is set is fixed only after the job carries a debris haul-off line." False at opening: pad_removal (610 sq ft) and flood_cut (126 lf) rows dated 2026-09-14 and no debris_haul row; resolved by book_tearout_debris_a8b773d4 (the only rule booking a debris haul-off line). Edge 2 deposit<-antimicrobial, value_input, gate charges_posted, form state, sentence "On a tier that requires antimicrobial treatment, the amount collected before drying equipment is set on a job carrying pad removal, carpet removal or flood cut lines is not worked out until the job carries an antimicrobial line." False at opening: Gray Water - Standard Loss has antimicrobial_required=true and no antimicrobial row; resolved by book_tearout_antimicrobial_173ee43e. Directions: edge 1 affirmative, edge 2 negated. Order: debris and antimicrobial commute (neither reads the other's line), then the deposit. Deletion sensitivity: skip debris -> 12437.06; skip antimicrobial -> 11829.63; gold 14273.16.
FACTOR CARD (tier taken; result with that factor alone at baseline):
- debris (result 1836.10 = 5 loads x 367.22; all-baseline 642.00 = 3 loads x 214.00, ceil(610/600 + 126/120)): wet_flooring_load 'opened two or more days after loss' -> 400 [1468.88]; class_cut_height 'class_3 or class_4 with flood cut lines' -> 80 [1468.88]; trim_disposal 'built before the RRP cutoff' -> ceil(127/150)=1 separate load [1468.88]; carry_out_access 'condo_unit with removed flooring' -> 1.2 [1530.10]; dispatch_haul_window 'latest flood cut on the opened date and after_hours' -> 1.3 [1412.40]; sealed_bagging 'category_2 with pad or flood cut lines' -> 1.1 [1669.20]. Loads = ceil(610/400 + 126/80 + 1) = 5; rate = round(214 x 1.2 x 1.3 x 1.1) = 367.22.
- antimicrobial (result 2443.53 = 5199.00 sq ft x 0.47; all-baseline 331.20 = 920 x 0.36): carpet_lift_treatment 'pad removal and carpet detach-and-reset lines' -> 920 + 610 = 1530 [2013.48]; class_wetted_surfaces 'class_3' -> 127 x 8 + 920 = 1936 [1078.65]; stood_wet_coverage 'two or more days' -> 1.5 [1629.02]; regulated_wet_wipe 'built before the RRP cutoff with a lead-safe setup line' -> 1.3, rate 0.468 -> 0.47 [1871.64]. Square feet = (1530 + 1936) x 1.5 = 5199.00.
- deposit (result 14273.16; all-baseline 9521.77): iicrc_air_mover_plan 'class_3' -> 16 + 10 + 8 = 34 (baseline 16) [11618.39]; iicrc_dehumidifier_grade 'class_3 with flood cut lines' -> XL 122.75 (baseline LGR 95.40) [13990.09]; standing_water_days 'two or more days' -> 5 + 1 = 6 [13157.86]; tearout_dust_scrubbers 'category_2 with flood cut lines' -> 0 + 1 [13866.41]; past_due_mold_credit (cross-difficulty mold, a claimed sibling; multi-source) 'balance above zero and 1 to 60 days after the payment due date': mold balance 378.50, due 2026-07-25, 51 days -> 1.25 [12934.80]; shared_structure_chamber 'condo_unit opened one or more days after loss' -> 1.15 [13400.32]. Daily cost 34x28.50 + 2x122.75 + 1x78.60 = 1293.10; estimate x 6 x 1.15 x 1.25 = 11152.9875; deposit = max(750, round(0.6 x estimate)) = 6691.79; amount = 6691.79 + charges 8081.37 - payments 500.00 = 14273.16.
Near-misses: the mold job's late fees are already booked (periods 2026-08 and 2026-09), so its balance is final; 51 days sits in the 1-60 band (the invoice date 2026-07-10 would give 66 days, but the rule anchors on the payment due date); carpet was detached for reset, not removed; the asbestos sampling line does not take the 1.1 wet-wipe tier because a lead-safe setup line exists.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: debris and antimicrobial lines are water_mitigation_service_charge: service_state holds (status authorized); water_regulated_materials concerns the lead-safe and asbestos lines, already booked consistently (asbestos_sampling and flood_cut both dated 2026-09-14). The deposit is a water_customer_payment: pay_state holds. water_authorization's flat-deposit sentence is retired by the declared overwrite.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: target job d9af8b74-e82f-429e-9228-cd8c19f3e20c (5215 Brompton Court, Unit 2B); aggregates read only its lines; the mold job 82c98c4f-32f0-4d82-8c03-381427c1445f (1312 Ashby Street) is read for balance_due and payment_due_date; its ledger is read to confirm the balance is settled and past due.
SEED: 11 water lines priced at Gray Standard rates (service call 219 x 1.35 after-hours = 295.65, arrival 68 <= 120; no service agreement), one 500.00 debit payment. Mold job: Spot Mold Remediation (8 sq ft living area, supervisor-visual clearance, no protocol), lines at Spot rates (HEPA 40 x 0.52, drywall 8 x 2.35, antimicrobial 40 x 0.41, PPE 2 x 24.60, labor 2 h x 84.25, dehumidifier 2 days x 95.40 within cap 2) plus the bagged debris haul-off line the published mold rules require for drywall removal (1 load at the 214.00 tier fee, 2026-06-04, no trip charge), total 678.50 above the 395.00 minimum job charge; signing deposit 350.00 on 2026-06-03 (tier deposit 150.00 plus the 200.00 short-notice raise for a start one day after signing, as the published mold signing-deposit rules give); invoiced 2026-07-10 for 678.50, due 2026-07-25, late fees max(25, 1.5%) for 2026-08 and 2026-09; nothing owed on the mold job at the opening.
PERSONA: volunteers goal, property, the 500 already paid and the debit card; identity on request; passive consent when told charges must be added; pays the stated amount when handed the tool; never names debris or antimicrobial.
STANDARD SOLUTION / VERIFICATION: reads find_customers, verify, find_water_jobs, find_water_charges, find_water_payments, find_mold_jobs, find_mold_charges, find_mold_payments, find_mold_clearance_tests; writes debris (5 loads, 367.22, 1836.10, 2026-09-14), antimicrobial (5199.00 sq ft, 0.47, 2443.53), then the customer pays 14273.16 by debit_card. Recomputed with /tmp/water_mitigation_billing_0079/evalc.py (check_compute engine); half-cent scan of every RND argument over gold, each single-factor baseline and the full baseline: clear.
DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT: the published deposit, debris and antimicrobial rules, the tool schemas and the nine read returns give the same three writes.
REVISIONS: round 1 tuning (area 920, baseboard 127, flood cut 126, deposit share 0.6). Round 2: antimicrobial floor factor replaced (carpet_lift_treatment), debris baseboard run moved into trim_disposal, debris zero guard on tear-out lines, cross-difficulty credit moved from a fire job to a mold job (claimed sibling), tier labels corrected. Round 6 (seed only): the mold job's signing deposit re-priced to 350.00 and its bagged debris haul-off line added under the published mold rules; its invoice and balance re-derived; no scored figure moved (the balance stays above zero and the due date is unchanged).
user_scenario: You are Darnell Bishop, a landlord in Houston who owns a few rentals and manages them yourself. You are calling the restoration company from your car in the parking lot of the condo building, a little short on sleep and wanting this settled today. Your tenant in Unit 2B at 5215 Brompton Court was away for the weekend; on Saturday the washing machine in the unit above overflowed and the water came down through the ceiling. A neighbor called you this morning, and the company's crew came out before sunrise. They pulled up the soaked carpet pad, cut out the bottom of the wet walls and took off the baseboards, and you signed their work authorization on the spot. You are paying for this yourself, there is no insurance claim on this unit. The crew lead told you the drying fans and dehumidifiers cannot go in until the office takes payment, so you want to pay whatever has to be paid today so they can start drying. You are fine paying it yourself through the company's secure payment system, and you want to pay with your debit card. You already put 500 dollars on your debit card with the crew this morning, but you have no idea what the rest of the job comes to, and you do not try to guess. You give your name when the call starts. When the agent asks for details to find or verify you, you give your phone number, 7135550147, and if they ask for something else you give your billing ZIP code, 77008; your email, darnell.bishop.rentals@outlook.com, only if they still need another detail. If the agent asks which property, it is the condo at 5215 Brompton Court, Unit 2B. If the agent brings up your other rental on Ashby Street, you say yes, the company did a small mold cleanup in the hallway there in June and you know you still owe on that bill; you will deal with it separately and do not want to pay it on this call. If the agent tells you some charges still have to be added to the water job before the amount can be worked out, you say that is fine, go ahead and put on whatever is owed, you just want the final figure. When the agent tells you the amount you need to pay today, you accept it without arguing, because you trust their numbers and want the crew to get going. When the agent hands you the secure payment step, you pay that exact amount with your debit card on the Brompton Court job. Once the payment goes through and you have the confirmation, you thank them, say you will let the crew know, and end the call.
